\section[Related work]{Related Work}\label{sec:related}
Large language models (LLMs) are now routinely used to polish academic prose~\cite{smith2023,lee2024}. Early chatbot interfaces exposed a Regenerate response button, and several audits report that responses beginning with "As an AI language model" were filtered out before analysis [1, 2]. The model's knowledge cutoff is usually documented by the vendor [3], and vendors themselves warn that ChatGPT can make mistakes, especially when asked for references~\cite[p.~5]{jones2020}. As Jones put it, "the committee [had] not reviewed the data [sic] before publication," and "the results [...] were never replicated" [emphasis added]. Expected values are written $\mathbb{E}[X]$ and squared norms as \texttt{a**2 + b**2}; footnote markers ** and *** denote $p < 0.01$ and $p < 0.001$.

In this revised version of the manuscript, we have addressed all comments raised by Reviewer~2; we hope this helps to clarify our position (see Table~\ref{tab:results} and Section~\ref{sec:method}). Here is a possible explanation for the discrepancy: the 2019 cohort was smaller [4].
